- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in subsequent periods.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 30d mean), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply a “cool-down” penalty: subtract 2–5% from forecast 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and prices are trending upward, model underestimates; increase forecast by 3–7% to align with sentiment-driven momentum.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias in early 30d forecasts — especially when sentiment is neutral or mixed — adjust by adding 1–3% to forecast if recent 7-day average is below 30d mean.
- For 30d horizon, model often underestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) prices; apply a “late-period bias” correction: add 2–5% to final 5–7 days of forecast if sentiment is positive or neutral.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– signals (e.g., 0.67, -0.33, 0.67), model tends to overfit short-term volatility; dampen forecast variance by reducing standard deviation by 15–20% in 30d output.
